# Telegram founder Pavel Durov says app now has 1B users, calls WhatsApp a ‘cheap, watered down imitation’

 Ivan Mehta 

10:43 AM PDT · March 19, 2025

Telegram founder Pavel Durov said today that the service now has more than 1 billion active users. This number is up from last year’s reported 950 million monthly active users.

Durov also noted that the company registered $547 million in profits last year. He had announced the company’s profitability in December but hadn’t provided any numbers at that time.

results.title: Telegram’s active users above one billion monthly — Durov -  Business & Economy - TASS
highlights:
# Telegram’s active users above one billion monthly — Durov 

"On average, each user opens Telegram 21 times daily and spends 41 minutes on the app every day," the messenger founder said

Pavel Durov

© AP Photo/ Tatan Syuflana

MOSCOW, March 19. /TASS/. The number of active monthly users of the Telegram app is much above one billion, founder of the messenger Pavel Durov wrote on his account.

"Telegram now has significantly over 1 billion monthly active users, becoming the second most popular messaging app in the world (excluding the China-specific WeChat)," Durov said.

"User engagement is also rising. On average, each user opens Telegram 21 times daily and spends 41 minutes on the app every day," the messenger founder said. At the same time, Telegram revenue growth "has exploded" and profits totaled $547 mln in 2024.

highlights:
As of May 2025, Telegram has 450 million daily active users. On average, each user spends three hours and 45 minutes per month on the app, with sessions lasting about one minute and 21 seconds. Roughly 53% of users are between 18 and 34 years old, reflecting the platform’s appeal to younger demographics. This aligns with broader trends: Millennials and Gen Z increasingly favor privacy-focused apps, and millennials, in particular, are more likely than other generations to regularly review and adjust their privacy settings.

...

By April 2025, Telegram ranked among the world’s top five most-downloaded apps, behind TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, and WhatsApp. Founder Pavel Durov reported in March 2025 that the platform had passed one billion monthly active users, up from 950 million monthly active users in mid-2024. Total downloads exceeded 2 billion in early 2025. Premium subscriptions grew rapidly in 2025, reaching 15 million in August 2025, compared with 4 million a month earlier.

...

Telegram has established itself as a major player in the global messaging market, surpassing one billion monthly active users as of March 2025 and achieving an estimated valuation of over $30 billion. This growth is driven by its privacy features, large group chat capabilities, and a feature-rich platform. The company became profitable in late 2024, with over $1 billion in revenue, fueled by premium subscriptions, advertising, and in-app monetization features like Telegram Stars. An IPO is under consideration to ensure independence and democratize access to Telegram's value.

results.title: Telegram Passes 1 Billion Monthly Active Users: What It Means
results.author: TechBloat Team
highlights:
Telegram says it passed one billion monthly active users in 2025. The milestone strengthens its position as a messaging, broadcast, creator, mini-app, and crypto platform—but does not prove it is larger than WhatsApp globally.

...

Facts about the article itself, counted from its text.

Telegram says it passed one billion monthly active users in 2025. The milestone was announced by founder Pavel Durov and is now repeated on Telegram’s official press page. It refers to monthly active users—not one billion registered accounts, daily users, or independently audited unique people.

...

In a March 2025 post, Durov said Telegram had “significantly over 1 billion monthly active users.” He also described Telegram as the second-most-popular messaging app outside China-specific WeChat and criticized WhatsApp as a “cheap, watered-down imitation.” Those rankings and characterizations are Durov’s, not independently established measurements.

...

Durov additionally claimed that the average Telegram user opened the app 21 times per day and spent 41 minutes using it daily. He said the company generated $547 million in profit during 2024. Because Telegram is privately held and does not publish the kind of detailed audited reporting expected from a listed company, those figures should remain attributed to Durov.

The key qualification is measurement. Telegram has not publicly supplied a transparent, independently audited methodology covering retention, regional distribution, duplicate accounts, bots, businesses, or the precise treatment of channels and automated activity. “Monthly active user” can mean someone who opened the app once during a 30-day period; it does not mean a person is online constantly.

...

Telegram reported roughly 900 million users in spring 2024, then announced 950 million monthly active users in July and said it was on track to reach one billion. An August 2024 Telegram update described the service as nearing that threshold. Moving from 950 million to more than one billion implies at least about 5.3% growth, although the dates and measurement windows are not perfectly comparable.

The trajectory is significant, but the older announcements sometimes used “users” less precisely than the later “monthly active users” wording. Downloads, registered accounts, monthly users, daily users, and unique individuals are different measures.

...

What remains unresolved is the independent verification of the exact user count and the quality of that activity. The evidence does not establish that Telegram has surpassed WhatsApp globally, that its profit figure is audited, or that its privacy and safety outcomes are superior. The most accurate summary is simple: Telegram says it passed one billion monthly active users in 2025, giving the company greater commercial leverage while increasing the demands placed on its transparency, moderation, and regulatory compliance.

### How many people use Telegram?

Telegram has more than 1 billion monthly active users. Pavel Durov announced the milestone on 19 March 2025 (TechCrunch). No newer official total has been published since; later statements say "over a billion".

The official milestones before that:

- 700 million monthly active users, June 2022 (Telegram blog)
- 800 million, reported by Durov in 2023 (CXOToday)
- 900 million, March 2024, in an interview with the Financial Times (Silicon UK)
- 950 million, July 2024 (TechCrunch)

results.title: Telegram Statistics 2026: Users, Revenue & Growth Data - Axis Intelligence
results.author: Axis Intelligence Research
highlights:
## Quick Answer: 

Telegram crossed 1 billion monthly active users in March 2025 — a milestone announced by Pavel Durov and first confirmed via investor documents — while simultaneously posting its first-ever annual profit of $540 million on $1.4 billion in revenue in 2024, per the Financial Times. In H1 2025, revenue grew 65% year over year to $870 million, but a $222 million net loss surfaced after a write-down of the company’s Toncoin holdings, which lost 69–73% of their value. The platform now processes over 15 billion messages daily and has 500 million daily active users.

...

1. Telegram reached 1 billion monthly active users in March 2025, up from 950 million in July 2024, adding roughly 50 million users over eight months at a pace of approximately 2.5 million new signups per day, per Pavel Durov’s public announcements and investor materials reviewed by the Financial Times.
2. Telegram generated $1.4 billion in revenue in 2024 and $540 million in profit — its first full-year profit in the three-year history of monetization — after posting a $173 million loss on $343 million in revenue in 2023, per investor presentation materials cited by the Financial Times in May 2025.
3. Per Axis Intelligence Research’s cross-source analysis of Financial Times investor documents, Telegram’s Toncoin Revenue Concentration Ratio™ (TRCR™) stood at 34.5% in H1 2025 — meaning over one-third of Telegram’s $870 million H1 2025 revenue depends on a single cryptocurrency asset whose price fell 69–73% in 2025, triggering a $222 million net loss despite $400 million in operating profit.
4. Telegram Premium subscribers grew 650% from 2 million in July 2023 to 15 million by May 2025, per Pavel Durov’s announcement on Telegram’s channel in May 2025 — yet premium users represent only 1.5% of Telegram’s 1 billion monthly active users, leaving the vast majority of the user base entirely unmonetized.
5. Following Pavel Durov’s arrest by French authorities in August 2024, Telegram’s fulfilled data requests to U.S. law enforcement jumped from 14 (affecting 108 users) in the first nine months of 2024 to 900 requests (affecting 2,253 users) for the full year — a post-arrest surge documented by TechCrunch in January 2025 and corroborated by the Freedom of the Press Foundation’s analysis of Telegram’s transparency bot data.

...

## How Many Users Does Telegram Have?

Telegram does not publish audited user statistics through a public filing. The figures below come from Pavel Durov’s public announcements, investor presentations reported by the Financial Times, and Telegram’s own app store listings.

### Monthly Active Users Growth Timeline

| Date | MAU | YoY Growth | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2014 (launch) | 35 million | — | Telegram / investor estimates |
| March 2018 | 200 million | — | Pavel Durov announcement |
| April 2020 | 400 million | — | Pavel Durov announcement |
| June 2022 | 700 million | — | Pavel Durov announcement |
| July 2024 | 950 million | — | Pavel Durov announcement |
| March 2025 | 1 billion | +5.3% YoY | Pavel Durov announcement |
| 2026 (est.) | 1 billion+ | — | Investor materials / Resourcera |

Source: Pavel Durov’s public posts on Telegram and X (formerly Twitter); investor materials cited by Financial Times.

From 35 million at launch in 2014 to 1 billion in March 2025 is an 11-year arc covering 2,757% growth, per multiple analyst calculations. The platform added 500 million users in the 36 months between April 2020 and June 2022 alone — a pandemic-era surge driven in part by WhatsApp’s controversial privacy policy update in January 2021, which triggered 25 million new Telegram signups in 72 hours, per Pavel Durov’s contemporaneous announcement.

The March 2025 milestone deserves a precision caveat: Telegram’s “active users” methodology is not publicly disclosed. Telegram does not distinguish between users who sent a message and users who opened the app. The 1 billion figure comes from investor materials, not an audited filing. Treat it as management’s figure, which is the appropriate standard — the same standard applied to WhatsApp’s 2 billion or Meta’s DAU disclosures.

...

### How many users does Telegram have in 2026?

Telegram crossed 1 billion monthly active users in March 2025, per Pavel Durov’s announcement corroborated by Financial Times reporting on investor materials. Estimates for 2026 range from 1 billion to slightly above, with the platform adding approximately 2.5 million new users daily. Daily active users reached approximately 500 million in late 2025, representing a 50% daily engagement rate of the monthly base.
